7564b46c5a.q: What is the operational capability and composition of a United States Navy super carrier?
7564b46c5a.a: The United States has 11 active duty aircraft carriers classified as super carriers, each displacing 100,000 tons with upwards of 5,000 people living aboard. They carry more than 70 aircraft, the majority of which are strike fighter aircraft. Nuclear propulsion allows them to operate for at least 25 years without refueling the ship itself, though aircraft still require fuel resupply. Aircraft carriers have been part of U.S. military capability for more than 100 years and played a huge role in World War II helping win the Pacific.

a09e925dd1.q: How did the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower improve from worst to best retention rate among all aircraft carriers?
a09e925dd1.a: When Rear Admiral Hill took command of the USS Dwight D. Eisenhower in 2023, the ship had poor morale and failed inspections. By implementing a leadership philosophy centered on loving and valuing personnel, providing mission and purpose, and constant recognition of accomplishments, the retention rate improved dramatically. Over a period of seven to eight months, the ship went from having the worst retention among all 11 aircraft carriers to number one retention rate right before deployment in 2023, demonstrating that the culture change strategy was working.

009c6a8e08.q: What are the core leadership pillars for building trust in high-stress military environments?
009c6a8e08.a: According to Rear Admiral Hill, the pillars for building a trusting team start with morale, which is distinct from happiness. Leaders must demonstrate that they love and value their people at all times, holding accountable those who do not. Second, leaders must give subordinates clear mission and purpose—something that drives them and gives them goals to look forward to. 8da62b6797.q: What role does vulnerability play in effective military and business leadership?
8da62b6797.a: Rear Admiral Hill emphasizes that leaders must acknowledge when they do not know something and ask for help from junior personnel. When a leader admits vulnerability and pulls in someone junior to explain how a component works, they empower that person to be part of the leadership team. On a 5,000-person aircraft carrier, it is impossible for one leader to know what is happening everywhere, so admitting vulnerability and soliciting expertise creates ownership and pride among team members. c193984065.q: How does the U.S. Navy's career management system handle personnel assignments across 350,000 active duty sailors?
c193984065.a: As Navy Career Manager, Rear Admiral Hill oversees a system that processes more than 1,000 personnel orders per day, totaling approximately 100,000 orders per year. The Navy manages a seashore rotation system where sailors move between ship duty, shore duty, repair facilities, instructor roles, recruiting positions, and back to sea. His office approaches this as concierge service, balancing sailor preferences with Navy operational needs. While the Navy cannot always grant requested assignments, especially when combat zones or critical staff positions require personnel, the goal is to link sailor preferences to Navy needs as often as possible.
